title: The Triangle of Critique
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article distinguishes critique from criticism and feedback, defining it as a deeper, analytical process that dissects a performance element by element using tools like video, process maps, or scorecards, rather than reacting to it in the moment. It introduces a "Triangle of Critique" with three essential qualities: precision about the drivers of performance, a focus on specific actionable behaviors rather than abstractions, and strict accountability to data rather than intuition. The piece notes that critique only lands when the person delivering it is seen as credible and expert, and argues that most organizations give plenty of feedback and criticism but rarely engage in genuine critique — a gap leaders can fill deliberately.
points: Critique differs from criticism and feedback — it's an analytical, time-intensive dissection of a performance using tools like video or process maps.
